correctness.rationale: For odd q, trace-zero Cayley–Hamilton and the anticommutator identity give E(X,Y)=4Q(X)Y−2tr(XY)X. Thus X=0 contributes only to zero; nonzero isotropic X has image its line and fiber q²; anisotropic X has image X-perp and fiber q. For a fixed nonzero isotropic target, its perpendicular plane has q(q−1) anisotropic vectors (nilpotent normal form gives c=0), in addition to the q−1 possible isotropic X in the target line. The split and nonsplit anisotropic normal forms give respectively bc and a²−tb² on the perpendicular plane, hence (q−1)² and q²−1 anisotropic X. The scalar equation a²+bc=t has q² solutions for t=0 and q(q+χ(t)) for t≠0, giving the claimed strata, zero fiber, and equal mass. These conjugacies are under GL₂, so no rational SL₂ conjugacy restriction is needed. In characteristic two the first bracket is scalar, so the second vanishes. The proof covers extensions and small fields; verify_engel.py is direct finite corroboration only, read but not rerun.
